name: Men's makeup tutorials

lead: Men's makeup tutorials are guides, often on YouTube, showing men how to use cosmetics such as concealer, foundation, bronzer and brow products for a natural result. They help looks by teaching how to even skin tone and define features.
Wikipedia notes male beauty bloggers on YouTube review products and teach makeup, with Patrick Starr and James Charles named as prominent examples.

paras: Tutorials typically start with skincare, then concealer and foundation, then brows and subtle contour; viewers practise on their own face.
Skin irritation or clogged pores are possible; patch tests and removal habits come up in instruction.

angle.text: Tutorials give men a method to cover blemishes and shadows and shape brows. Results depend on practice.

lead: Men's makeup tutorials are instruction content targeted at men using cosmetics. Their growth tracks the male cosmetics market, where brands such as Nivea, Chanel and Tom Ford sell men's lines and YouTube creators teach makeup.[1]

Wikipedia reports that men aged 18 to 34 are the most likely users and that men use products to cover blemishes; it also cites survey figures showing far more men using skincare than regarding makeup as important.[1]

paras: Men have used cosmetics since ancient Egypt, and a modern market re-emerged with 1930s film and grew from the late 1990s.[1]
Patrick Starr and James Charles are named among prominent male beauty creators.[1]
